title: Kernel Slate Autotuner: Microbench Fingerprinting for Mixed-SeqLen Routing
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: The serving runtime currently picks kernels based on static cost models that do not generalize across mixed sequence-length workloads and heterogeneous GPU generations. This causes suboptimal per-token latency and cost for real traffic that mixes short prefill histories with long decode tails.

Goal: Build a lightweight 'kernel slate' autotuner that 1) fingerprints request profiles via microbench probes, 2) maintains a compact per-arch/seqlen slate of candidate kernels, and 3) quickly routes requests to the best-performing kernel with bounded exploration overhead. The solution must be safe (no increased p99 regressions) and roll outable via canary.

Approach overview:
- Offline microbench harness: run a focused set of tiny microbenchmarks across GPU families (A100, H100, RTX) and representative sequence-length buckets (e.g., prefill 64/256, decode 1/32/128). Produce a kernel performance matrix (latency, memory, occupancy) per model family and quantization profile.
- Fingerprint design: derive a compact request fingerprint combining seqlen histogram (prefill vs decode), kv-cache hit ratio estimate, and estimated batch compaction (from batching rules). Hash into a small namespace to index kernel slates.
- Slate representation: for each (arch, model-shape, fingerprint-bucket) maintain top-3 kernel candidates with an empirical score (EWMA of token-latency and cost). Store metadata for safe fallbacks (stable kernel, exploration count, last-updated).
- Online routing + probe policy: route most requests to slate.best; probabilistically probe alternative kernels at a low decayed rate per-bucket. Probes are micro-burst experiments that are constrained by p99 budget. Use contextual bandit with latency regret threshold to adapt exploration.
- Integration points: serving runtime kernel registry, scheduler hook for prefill vs decode phase, runtime telemetry to export per-kernel metrics into Console dashboards, and rollout flags for canarying.

Non-goals: full model-retraining-aware kernel selection; exhaustive cross-GPU redistribution (this is per-host/instance-aware).
acceptance_criteria: Offline harness produces kernel performance matrix for at least 3 GPU families and 4 seqlen buckets documented in a Confluence page.
Runtime can compute fingerprint and choose a kernel slate for incoming requests with <200 microsecond overhead in the hot path.
Online probe policy demonstrates exploration without increasing p99 latency by >5% in canary traffic (measurement via Console or dedicated dashboard).
Deployment includes feature flag + canary rollout plan and an automatic rollback trigger when p99 or error-rate thresholds are exceeded.
Documentation: operator runbook describing slate eviction, cache warm restart behavior, and metrics to monitor (per-slate latency, probe-rate, regret score).
